howDoI.q: How do I make a key that is worth more than one?
How do I make a door that costs more?
How do I let the player keep what a door does not take?
How do I make a stronger key open every weaker door?
How do I make small keys add up to a big one?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Stronger Keys is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Up and Down climb a ladder. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on. There is nothing to fight and nothing that hurts.

pages.head: Level 1: Small Key, Big Door
pages.html:
Level 1: Small Key, Big Door

A bronze key lies on the ground, with a sign saying it is worth 1. Walk right to the silver door, which costs 2, and bump it: it stays shut. A ladder climbs to a ledge with the silver key, worth 2. Take it, come back and walk into the door. It opens, and there is still one bronze key's worth left, which pays for the plain bronze door beyond. The EXIT → sign points to the way out.

Coins are worth ten points each. There are nine, and a key is worth 25.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The keys. Open power.bbl in the blocks editor and pick key_bronze. On its Touch tab, Effect counter is counter 20 and Effect amount is 1, and Becomes block is sky, so the key is gone once you have it. key_silver is the same with an amount of 2 and key_gold with 3. A stronger key is only a bigger number. The teeth drawn on each key match its amount.
  • The doors. gate_silver is solid on every side, so it stops you. Its Effect counter is also counter 20, but its Effect amount is −2. A counter from 20 up will not go to zero or less, so a touch that cannot be paid for does nothing. With only the bronze key the door stays shut. With the silver key the touch pays 2, and Becomes block turns the door into sky.
  • The change. A door takes its price and nothing more. With the bronze and silver keys the count is 3, the silver door takes 2, and 1 is left for gate_bronze, whose amount is −1.
  • Why you cannot jump over a door. Each door is one block high, with an arch block above it that you walk under, and a wall of brick from there up to the top of the level.
  • The counter itself. Open hero.chr in the character editor. Counter 20 starts at 1, which the game shows as none carried.
  • The signs. Each sign is a few ordinary blocks side by side, with the words drawn in their pictures. Change the words in the blocks editor and play again.

pages.head: Level 2: One Gold Key
pages.html:
Level 2: One Gold Key

The gold key, worth 3, waits on a ledge up a ladder near the start. A bronze door (cost 1) and a silver door (cost 2) stand ahead. Walk into the bronze door and then the silver one: the one gold key pays for both. A stronger key opens every weaker door.

Coins are worth ten points each. There are ten, and a key is worth 25.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • One key, two doors. Open two.map in the map editor. key_gold adds 3 to counter 20. The bronze door takes 1, which leaves 2, and the silver door takes 2, which leaves none. Either door could come first, because 3 pays for both.
  • Spending is the catch. A stronger key does not open weaker doors for free: each door takes its own price. A gold key spent on a gold door (3) leaves nothing for the others.
  • The ladder. A column of ladder blocks beside a ledge of grass over dirt.

pages.head: Level 3: Keys Add Up
pages.html:
Level 3: Keys Add Up

A gold door costs 3. Walk into it with only the bronze key (1) and it stays shut. The silver key (2) is on a ledge up a ladder. Carry both and the count is 3: enough. Small keys add up.

Coins are worth ten points each. There are eight, and a key is worth 25.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • The gold door. Open power.bbl and pick gate_gold. Its Effect counter is counter 20 and its Effect amount is −3. It needs 3 in the count, whichever keys made it. The bronze key adds 1 and the silver key adds 2, so together they pay.
  • Why not one key per door? A counter only holds a number. It does not remember which keys made it. To keep two kinds of key apart, give them separate counters, as Keys and Doors does.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

  • A counter holds whole numbers up to 32766. Past that a key just fills it, so a ladder cannot have steps taller than the counter, and a price above 32766 can never be paid.
  • A door takes all of its price or nothing. It cannot take half a key.
  • A counter cannot tell which keys made it. Bronze and silver together look the same as a gold key to the door.
  • The game cannot show the number. Only the signs and the pictures on the keys say what is worth what.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Open power.bbl and change a door's Effect amount, say the silver door from −2 to −3, then play level 1 again. Add a fourth rung: a key worth 4 and a door that takes 4. Save the copy and play it.
